plates.side_label: 98% TRYPSIN ENZYME DESTRUCTION VS BANTING'S DUCT-LIGATION METHOD
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked comparison diagram contrasts a whole ground pancreas (98% acinar trypsin enzymes digesting and destroying the 1%–2% islet insulin) against Frederick Banting's 31 October 1920 duct-ligation method (acinar enzyme cells degenerate over 6–8 weeks, leaving pure insulin-producing Islets of Langerhans intact).

teach_overlay.label: WHOLE GROUND PANCREAS (98% TRYPSIN DESTROYS INSULIN) VS DUCT LIGATION (ISLETS INTACT)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked comparison diagram on period paper showing a whole ground pancreas (98% acinar trypsin enzymes destroying the 1%–2% islet insulin) vs Banting's 31 October 1920 duct-ligation method (acinar cells degenerate, leaving pure Islets of Langerhans intact)
teach_overlay.scale: ninety-eight percent of the pancreas is a factory of meat-dissolving digestive enzymes — so grinding up a whole pancreas was like throwing a delicate hormone key straight into a vat of acid
